title: Question 1.1
statement_text: Is it true that for every (fixed) integer $t > 0$, the 3-coloring problem can be solved in polynomial time when restricted to the class of $P_t$-free graphs?
context_text: $P_t$ denotes the path on $t$ vertices, and a graph $G$ is $H$-free if no induced subgraph of $G$ is isomorphic to $H$; polynomial time means polynomial in $|V(G)|$ for the input graph $G$. The $k$-coloring problem asks whether the input graph admits a proper coloring with $k$ colors. A known result from the literature states that if, for some fixed $k>2$, the $k$-coloring problem is polynomial-time solvable on $H$-free graphs, then every connected component of $H$ is a path. For $k=3$ the converse may hold (it is known to fail for $k>4$), and this question asks exactly that for $H=P_t$, since every graph whose components are paths is an induced subgraph of a long path. Known positive results include polynomial-time list-3-coloring of $P_7$-free graphs, of $(P_5+P_2)$-free and $(P_4+P_3)$-free graphs, and a subexponential algorithm for $P_t$-free graphs. The present paper shows that list-3-coloring (hence 3-coloring) is polynomial for $(P_6+rP_3)$-free graphs, where $P_6+rP_3$ is the disjoint union of a $P_6$ and $r$ copies of $P_3$, and that $k$-coloring of $(P_5+P_2)$-free graphs is NP-hard for $k\ge5$.
notes: The question has no explicit attribution citation in the header; it is recorded as a standing open problem in the field by the paper's authors. Full paper text was truncated in the supplied PDF extraction, so later sections could not be checked for additional conjectural statements.
